description: Plugins installed from the catalog run as isolated processes in a macOS sandbox, never inside the app. Nothing third-party runs until you turn the master switch on, and turning it off stops every one of them. Safe mode stops them all at once without removing anything. A plugin you install starts off with no permissions and asks again when its code changes.
examples: Install a plugin from Warez: it lands switched off with no permissions, you tick what it asks for, and it runs only while the master switch is on.
Turn the switch off before handing your computer to someone: every third-party plugin stops within a moment.
how_to: Open the plugins page and flip third-party plugins on; the note beside it says sandbox ready, not checked yet, or unavailable with the reason.
Flip it off to stop every third-party plugin; installed ones and their data stay.
If the note says safe mode is on, none run until safe mode is lifted.
name: Third-party plugins switch
summary: one owner switch, off by default, that decides whether any plugin installed from the catalog may run, with a sandbox check and a safe mode.
where: The plugins page, the third-party plugins row at the top.
